paragraphs.en: Last year marked the third year in a row of when Indonesia’s bleak rate of deforestation has slowed in pace. One reason for the turnaround may be the country’s antipoverty program.
paragraphs.zh: 去年，印度尼西亚严峻的森林砍伐势头连续第三年放缓。这一转变的原因之一，可能是该国的扶贫计划。

paragraphs.en: In 2007, Indonesia started phasing in a program that gives money to its poorest residents under certain conditions, such as requiring people to keep kids in school or get regular medical care. Called conditional cash transfers or CCTs, these social assistance programs are designed to reduce inequality and break the cycle of poverty.They’re already used in dozens of countries worldwide. In Indonesia, the program has provided enough food and medicine to substantially reduce severe growth problems among children.
paragraphs.zh: 2007年，印度尼西亚开始逐步实施一项计划，在满足某些条件的情况下向最贫困的居民发放现金，例如要求他们让孩子继续上学，或定期接受医疗保健。这些被称为“有条件现金转移支付”（CCT）的社会救助计划旨在减少不平等，打破贫困循环。全球已有数十个国家采用这种计划。在印度尼西亚，该计划提供了足够的食物和药品，使儿童严重生长发育问题大幅减少。

paragraphs.en: But CCT programs don’t generally consider effects on the environment. In fact, poverty alleviation and environmental protection are often viewed as conflicting goals, says Paul Ferraro , an economist at Johns Hopkins University.
paragraphs.zh: 但有条件现金转移支付计划通常不会考虑对环境的影响。约翰斯·霍普金斯大学经济学家保罗·费拉罗说，事实上，扶贫与环境保护常常被视为相互冲突的目标。

paragraphs.en: That’s because economic growth can be correlated with environmental degradation, while protecting the environment is sometimes correlated with greater poverty.However, those correlations don’t prove cause and effect. The only previous study analyzing causality, based on an area in Mexico that had instituted CCTs, supported the traditional view. There, as people got more money, some of them may have more cleared land for cattle to raise for meat,Ferraro says.
paragraphs.zh: 这是因为经济增长可能与环境恶化相关，而保护环境有时又与贫困加剧相关。然而，这些相关性并不能证明因果关系。此前唯一一项分析因果关系的研究，以墨西哥一个实施了有条件现金转移支付计划的地区为对象，其结果支持了传统观点。费拉罗说，在那里，随着人们获得更多钱，一些人可能开垦了更多土地，用来饲养供肉食用的牛。

paragraphs.en: Such programs do not have to negatively affect the environment, though. Ferraro wanted to see if Indonesia’s poverty-alleviation program was affecting deforestation. Indonesia has the third-largest area of tropical forest in the world and one of the highest deforestation rates.
paragraphs.zh: 不过，此类计划不一定会对环境产生负面影响。费拉罗想看看，印度尼西亚的扶贫计划是否影响了森林砍伐。印度尼西亚的热带森林面积位居世界第三，森林砍伐率也位居世界前列。

paragraphs.en: Ferraro analyzed satellite data showing annual forest loss from 2008 to 2012— including during Indonesia’s phase-in of the antipoverty program—in 7,468 forested villages across 15 provinces. “We see that the program is associated with a 30 percent reduction in deforestation,” Ferraro says.
paragraphs.zh: 费拉罗分析了卫星数据，这些数据记录了15个省中7468个有森林覆盖的村庄在2008年至2012年间的年度森林损失情况，其中包括印度尼西亚逐步推行扶贫计划的时期。“我们发现，这项计划与森林砍伐减少30%有关，”费拉罗说。

paragraphs.en: That’s likely because the rural poor are using the money as makeshift insurance policies against inclement weather, Ferraro says. Typically, if rains are delayed, people may clear land to plant more rice to supplement their harvests.
paragraphs.zh: 费拉罗说，这很可能是因为农村贫困人口把这笔钱当作应对恶劣天气的临时保险。通常，如果雨季迟迟不来，人们可能会开垦土地，种植更多水稻以弥补收成的不足。

paragraphs.en: Whether this research translates elsewhere is anybody’s guess.Ferraro suggests the results may transfer to other parts of Asia, due to commonalities such as the importance of growing rice and market access.And regardless of transferability, the study shows that what’s good for people may also be good for the environment. Even if this program didn’t reduce poverty, Ferraro says, “the value of the avoided deforestation just for carbon dioxide emissions alone is more than the program costs.”
paragraphs.zh: 这项研究的结论能否适用于其他地方，谁也说不准。费拉罗认为，由于水稻种植的重要性以及市场可及性等方面存在共性，这些结果可能适用于亚洲其他地区。不论其结论能否推广，这项研究都表明，对人有益的事也可能有益于环境。费拉罗说，即使这个计划没有减少贫困，“仅从二氧化碳排放的角度看，避免森林砍伐所产生的价值就已经超过了计划本身的成本。”
